samples.question: Exactly one stroke in this picture is a long unbroken wire: it runs straight across, turns at its end, comes back the other way, and does this until it has made five horizontal passes, one under the next. Five short vertical rails, drawn in a different colour, stand across those passes, so the wire meets a rail at twenty-five crossings, five on every pass. At each crossing the wire does one of exactly two things: it arches up over the rail in a small raised hop, or it cuts straight across at the level of the pass. One end of the wire carries a small filled round bead just inside the wire's tip; the other end has no bead. Carry out this operation: start at the beaded end and walk along the wire to its far end, so you travel the five passes one after another; write the first pass you travel into row 1 of a 5 by 5 grid, the second into row 2, and so on to row 5; within each pass, fill that row's five columns left to right in the order you meet its five crossings as you travel, so a pass walked from right to left fills its row starting from the crossing you reach first; then mark every grid position whose crossing was a raised hop. Exactly 9 of the 25 positions are marked. The marked positions form one symbol on the 5 by 5 grid: 'ell' is the whole left column together with the whole bottom row; 'tee' is the whole top row together with the centre column below it; 'eff' is the top row's first four positions, the left column down to row 4, and the middle row's first three positions; 'zed' is the top row's first three positions, then a step down and left through row 2 column 4, row 3 column 3 and row 4 column 2, then the bottom row's last three positions. The rails, the scattered marks elsewhere in the picture and the wire's own position on the page are decoration; only which crossings are hopped, taken in walking order from the beaded end, decides the symbol. Which symbol do the marked positions form? Answer with exactly one of: eff, ell, tee, zed.
